assessment.nobel_worthiness: An invention in the literal Nobel sense: a unipolar semiconductor laser whose wavelength is set by layer thickness through band-engineered intersubband transitions, not by the bandgap. It opened the mid-infrared and terahertz ranges to compact sources and is now used in trace-gas sensing, spectroscopy and security. The original 1994 device was demonstrated experimentally, and I find that the clearest kind of case.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 Bell Labs team (Faist, Capasso, Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson, Cho) built the first device. Capasso led the concept, Faist realized and drove the early development, and Cho's molecular beam epitaxy growth made the layered structures possible. The supplied credit supports a fair three-person configuration, though I would check the record on who first proposed intersubband lasing (Kazarinov and Suris, 1971).
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent confirmation, room-temperature continuous-wave operation, and widespread commercial and scientific use. Recognition is well within the usual timeframe, and some may argue it is overdue.
uncertainties: The 1971 Kazarinov-Suris proposal could weaken the originality claim if the committee reads it as prior art.
Cho's role is as growth enabler rather than conceptual inventor, so his inclusion is debatable.
Other Bell Labs co-inventors (e.g. Carlo Sirtori) are not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)F(x) in 2008 started an entirely new family of high-temperature superconductors with a different electronic structure from the cuprates. It is a materials discovery that can be seen and measured, and it is experimentally verified many times over. It gave a second platform for studying unconventional pairing.
assessment.attribution: My reading of the original-experiment principle is that Hosono's group reported the first iron-pnictide superconductor (an initial Tc of about 26 K), which started the field. Chen and Zhao reported higher Tc in the weeks that followed. By my own stated criteria these are the quick follow-ups that raised Tc, not the original discovery, so I would propose Hosono alone, and I would want the committee to confirm the chronology.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of replication, with a mature field and well-established material families. The pairing mechanism is still debated, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether the pairing mechanism being unresolved weakens the case for the committee.
Hosono's earlier unrelated work (transparent oxide semiconductors) might compete for the credit narrative.
Priority questions in 2008 between Hosono and the rapid Chinese follow-ups need to be checked against the record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent manipulation of a single nitrogen-vacancy centre at room temperature turned a point defect in diamond into a quantum sensor and spin qubit. The tool lets people measure magnetic fields, temperature and strain at the nanoscale in conditions that were inaccessible before, including in living cells. It is very much the kind of instrument that opens a door.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group first detected single NV centres optically (1997) and Jelezko demonstrated coherent control of a single spin (2004). I would propose these two. Lukin's contributions to sensing protocols and quantum-network applications are large, but they are later and more broadly applied, so I would not add him unless the committee argues the sensing step is the decisive one.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed and extended the technique, and applications in magnetometry, bioimaging and quantum networks are growing. The basic discoveries are mature, while the applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be for single-spin detection, coherent control, or sensing applications.
Gruber et al. 1997 co-authorship and other early contributors (e.g. Awschalom's group on spin control) are not credited.
Overlap with other solid-state spin work and the broader solid-state spin literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators in 2005, followed by the experimental observation of edge-channel transport in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, founded a whole field. The experiment is a clean transport measurement, and subsequent ARPES work on 3D topological insulators confirmed the broader picture. The impact on how we classify phases of matter is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction. Molenkamp's group did the original experiment, though it was a response to the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal for HgTe, and BHZ are not among the credited names. This makes the fair configuration awkward, as I would worry about the theory side without a full set of theorists. I would propose the three credited people but flag the gap.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: nearly twenty years of independent confirmation across materials and techniques. There is no question about timeliness; the issue is attribution, not readiness.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction, and for the experimental 3D topological insulator discoveries (Hsieh, Hasan and others).
Whether the committee should split the 2D (QSH) and 3D steps.
The practical benefit for humanity is still prospective rather than realized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics placed superconducting artificial atoms inside on-chip microwave resonators, which gives strong coupling, dispersive readout and the architecture that almost all superconducting quantum processors now use. It is a central tool of the quantum technology field and a good instrument-based advance.
assessment.attribution: Blais et al. (2004) proposed the architecture and Wallraff et al. (2004), working with Schoelkopf's team, demonstrated strong coupling. Girvin is a key co-author of the theory. The supplied list has four names, so I would take the experimental pair plus Blais, noting that the allocation between Wallraff, Schoelkopf and the theory authors needs careful archival work.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and extension in many labs. The 2025 prize recognized circuit-based macroscopic quantum tunnelling, which is closely related, and so the committee may feel that this theme was just recently acknowledged.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may argue for waiting.
Credit across Blais, Girvin, Wallraff and Schoelkopf is hard to limit to three, and I did not verify the exact historical priority.
Several earlier ideas (Cooper-pair box, Nakamura's qubit) are part of the same story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength idea with many atoms interrogated at once, and it reaches fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This is a measurement-tool advance that has changed metrology and tests of fundamental physics, and it is the front-runner for a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2003 and demonstrated the first clock; Ye's group pushed the accuracy and stability records and built a broad programme. Two names are a natural prize configuration. I would give Katori precedence for the original invention.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced at several national labs, with performance still improving. The Nobel Committee honored Hall and Hänsch (frequency combs) in 2005 and Wineland in 2012 for ion clocks, so the field is established, but the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion-based clocks and the 2005 frequency-comb prize makes the incremental novelty arguable.
Ye's credit for the clock itself versus the frequency-comb and ultracold-molecule work is not settled in my mind.
Whether the redefinition of the second should first happen.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 measurement of a non-zero theta-13 through reactor antineutrino disappearance was a precise, decisive experiment that completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the way to searching for CP violation in the lepton sector. It is clear, quantitative and verified by several experiments.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) reported the effect almost simultaneously, with Double Chooz in parallel and T2K indicating it with accelerator beams. Fair credit is a real problem, since large collaborations and several competing teams were involved, and the committee must be absolutely sure of the leaders. The supplied names are a reasonable proposal but not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent experiments, and the value of theta-13 is now measured precisely. The result is mature and the topic builds on the 2015 prize for neutrino oscillations.
uncertainties: Double Chooz and T2K contributions are not in the credited list.
Large-collaboration leadership and who made the decisive contributions is not easy to determine.
Possible concern that the 2015 prize already covers the oscillation story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, created a controllable platform for strongly correlated physics. A twist angle is a new knob, and it opens a door to phenomena that could not be accessed before.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) made the theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group did the original experiments (Cao et al. 2018). The three credited names form a natural configuration. Other experimental groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani) and other theorists contributed important steps that may need separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Experimental results have been reproduced widely, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and many correlated states is still under discussion. It may be premature compared with candidates that have longer track records.
uncertainties: The nature of the superconducting state remains unsettled.
Applications and benefit for humanity are not yet realized.
Several other groups and theorists contributed to the magic-angle story and are not credited.
